stem: Cobalt is a transition element with atomic number 27. Cobalt forms ions with charges of $+2$ and $+3$. Both these ions form complexes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Complete the electronic configurations of a Co atom and a $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: One $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ion can form a tetrahedral complex ion with four $\text{Cl}^-$ ions. This complex is blue.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: What is meant by the term complex ion?

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Draw the tetrahedral complex ion formed by one $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ion with four $\text{Cl}^-$ ions. Your drawing should clearly show three-dimensional shape, and should include the overall charge on the ion.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why many transition metal complexes are coloured.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Using ideas from your answer to (iii) suggest why the colour of the complex formed by one $\text{Co}^{2+}$ ion with four $\text{Cl}^-$ ions is blue.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Describe the colour change that occurs when water is added to blue crystals of the cobalt(II)-chloride complex. Name the type of reaction responsible for this colour change.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Use the Data Booklet to suggest a suitable oxidising agent for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between $\text{Co}^{2+}$ and the oxidising agent you chose in (d)(i).
